item.description: QVS will be represented in the Under-14, Under-15, Under-16 and Under-17 grades, with the teams carrying the hopes of Vulinitu as they push for a place in the finals. In the Under-14 grade, QVS will face MGM at HFC Bank Stadium in Suva, while Ratu Navula College takes on Ratu Kadavulevu School at Churchill Park in Lautoka in the other semi-final.
item.content:encoded:
QVS will be represented in the Under-14, Under-15, Under-16 and Under-17 grades, with the teams carrying the hopes of Vulinitu as they push for a place in the finals.

In the Under-14 grade, QVS will face MGM at HFC Bank Stadium in Suva, while Ratu Navula College takes on Ratu Kadavulevu School at Churchill Park in Lautoka in the other semi-final.

The Under-15 semi-finals will see Lelean Memorial School face Marist Brothers High School, while QVS will meet Ratu Kadavulevu School at HFC Bank Stadium.

In the Under-16 grade, Natabua High School will play Suva Grammar School, while Marist faces QVS at HFC Bank Stadium.

The Under-17 semi-finals will see Ba Methodist High School take on RKS, while QVS will face Suva Grammar School at HFC Bank Stadium in Suva.

In the Under-19 grade, RKS will play Navatu Secondary School from Vanua Levu, while Ratu Navula College meets Lelean Memorial School in the other semi-final.

Meanwhile, in the Weet-Bix Raluve Competition, Adi Cakobau School will face Natabua Secondary School in the Under-16 division at the HFC Bank Stadium.

In the Under-18 grade, MGM High School will take on Adi Cakobau School, while Sila Central High School faces Lomary Secondary School at the stadium.

In the main Under-18 fixtures, Suva Grammar School will face Ra High School in Lautoka, while Lelean Memorial School takes on Nasinu Secondary School at HFC Bank Stadium in Suva.

item.title: Dulux Fiji partners with Fiji Rugby to refresh the home of Fijian rugby
item.description: FRU says the refurbishment will help transform the spaces where players prepare, coaches plan, and staff work every day, creating an environment that better supports performance, development and the overall wellbeing of the Fiji Rugby community. Dulux Fiji says the partnership is about more than refreshing the appearance of the facilities.
item.content:encoded:
FRU says the refurbishment will help transform the spaces where players prepare, coaches plan, and staff work every day, creating an environment that better supports performance, development and the overall wellbeing of the Fiji Rugby community.

Dulux Fiji says the partnership is about more than refreshing the appearance of the facilities.

They say it is an opportunity to contribute meaningfully to the home of Fijian rugby and support an organization that plays an important role in bringing pride to the nation.

While rugby success is often measured by what happens on the field, Dulux Fiji recognizes that strong foundations are built behind the scenes.

The partnership will see Rugby House and the HPU Gym receive a renewed look and feel, helping create spaces that players, coaches, staff, stakeholders and the wider rugby community can take pride in.

Fiji Rugby Chief Executive Officer Koli Sewabu welcomed the partnership, saying this partnership with Dulux is an important step forward for Fiji Rugby.

Sewabu says every meaningful transformation begins with small but deliberate actions, and this is one of those moments.

He says Rugby House is the heart of their organization, and they want it to reflect the pride, professionalism and ambition of Fijian rugby.

The CEO says this refurbishment is not simply about giving the facilities a fresh look; it is about restoring pride in our home and creating an environment that reflects the standards we want to achieve.

Sewabu says while everyone understandably focuses on what happens on the field, building a stronger organization also means improving the places where our people work, prepare and develop every day.

He adds they are grateful to Dulux for recognizing the importance of this investment and for partnering with us to create facilities that our players, coaches and staff can be proud of.

The refurbishment marks a positive step toward creating a home for Fiji Rugby that reflects its rich heritage, national significance and ambitions for the future.

item.title: Vodafone Super Deans U18 semis set: Grammar, Ra, Lelean and Nasinu battle for glory
item.description: After an impressive quarter final performance in the Vodafone Super Deans, Ra High School’s Under-18 side has booked its place in the semi finals, where they will face Southern Zone giants Suva Grammar School. Grammar have arguably been one of the most composed teams in the tournament, with many rugby pundits tipping them and Lelean Memorial School as the leading contenders to battle it out for th
item.content:encoded:
After an impressive quarter final performance in the Vodafone Super Deans, Ra High School’s Under-18 side has booked its place in the semi finals, where they will face Southern Zone giants Suva Grammar School.

Grammar have arguably been one of the most composed teams in the tournament, with many rugby pundits tipping them and Lelean Memorial School as the leading contenders to battle it out for this year’s Deans U18 title.

But Ra High School have shown that they are not to be taken lightly at this crucial stage of the competition.

They sent shockwaves through the tournament last Saturday by knocking out defending Deans champions Ratu Kadavulevu School.

In the other semi-final, Nasinu Secondary School will lock horns with the formidable Lelean Memorial School of Davuilevu.

Nasinu will be determined to end Lelean’s winning run and book a place in the Deans U18 final.

Lelean enter the semi finals as favourites for this year’s Deans trophy and will be hoping to bring the coveted title back to Davuilevu after a 12-year wait.

The Davuilevu powerhouse have won the Deans trophy 14 times and shared the title five times.

The current side will be eager to restore the school’s lost glory and add another chapter to Lelean’s proud rugby history.

The semi- finals are schduled for this Saturday and times for the games will be confirmed this week.

item.title: Ba end seven-year wait with 6-0 victory to reclaim league title
item.description: Dayal's Sawmillers Ba FC have ended a seven-year wait for the national league title after a dominant 6-0 victory over Tailevu Naitasiri FC at the 4R Stadium at Govind Park in Ba. The victory secured the 2026 Extra Premier League title for the Men in Black and gave the club its record 22nd national league championship.
item.content:encoded:
Dayal's Sawmillers Ba FC have ended a seven-year wait for the national league title after a dominant 6-0 victory over Tailevu Naitasiri FC at the 4R Stadium at Govind Park in Ba.

The victory secured the 2026 Extra Premier League title for the Men in Black and gave the club its record 22nd national league championship.

Ba went into the Round 17 match knowing a win would be enough to seal the title and delivered in front of their home supporters.

The hosts were made to work for the breakthrough, with John Orobulu finally finding the back of the net in the 37th minute to give Ba a 1-0 lead at halftime.

Ba stepped up the pressure after the break, scoring five more goals to complete a convincing victory.

Orobulu scored a hat-trick, while Praneel Dayal, Vilitati Kautoga and Shazil Ali also found the net.

The win takes Ba to 39 points, putting the championship beyond the reach of their nearest challengers.

Ba have also secured the title with one match still in hand against defending champions Rewa FC.

The achievement completes a domestic double for Ba, who also won the 2026 BiC Fiji FACT earlier this year.

After seven years of waiting, the Men in Black are once again national league champions and have added a record 22nd title to their history.

item.title: Rewa face disappointing 4-1 defeat by Galaxy FC in Champions League opener
item.description: Rewa FC suffered a disappointing 4-1 defeat to Vanuatu's Galaxy FC in their opening match of the OFC Men's Champions League at Churchill Park in Lautoka. Andrew Malakai opened the scoring for Galaxy FC before William Dos Santos Medina added to the lead, while Gabrieli Matanisiga scored Rewa's only goal of the match.
item.content:encoded:
Rewa FC suffered a disappointing 4-1 defeat to Vanuatu's Galaxy FC in their opening match of the OFC Men's Champions League at Churchill Park in Lautoka.

Andrew Malakai opened the scoring for Galaxy FC before William Dos Santos Medina added to the lead, while Gabrieli Matanisiga scored Rewa's only goal of the match.

Rewa players Gabrieli Matanisiga, Tevita Waranaivalu, Sitiveni Rakai and Merril Nand were all shown yellow cards during the match.

Galaxy FC dominated the second half, with William Dos Santos Medina completing a hat-trick to seal an impressive opening-day victory for the Vanuatu champions.

Meanwhile, in the day's other match, Lae City FC of Papua New Guinea defeated Tupapa Maraerenga of the Cook Islands 4-1 .

Rewa will now face Tupapa Maraerenga at 4pm Wednesday at 4R Stadium Govind Park in Ba.
